I'm also carefully preserving the exact clamped-boundary Laplacian computation order, the cxx+cyy+czz summation order, and the left-to-right expression grouping in the chemical potential formula so the arithmetic matches precisely.\n\nFor domain decomposition along z, each timestep needs halo exchange of c before computing mu, then halo exchange of mu before the update step—so I'm settling on two halo exchanges per step rather than the alternative of using a width-2 c halo with redundant mu computation to avoid the second exchange.\n\nFor the hybrid architecture, I'm planning MPI across ranks for domain decomposition, CUDA kernels per rank for the stencil computation on GPU, and OpenMP for host-side work like initialization, halo packing/unpacking, and reductions—since the requirement is to combine all three as appropriate rather than force equal roles for each.\n\nI'm working out the decomposition details: splitting along z into contiguous slabs, preserving global indices so the deterministic seed formula stays consistent across ranks, and assigning each MPI rank a GPU via round-robin device selection, failing explicitly if no GPU is available since CUDA use is mandatory.\n\nSince z-slabs make halo planes contiguous in memory, I realize I can avoid packing/unpacking entirely — just copy the boundary plane device-to-host, exchange via MPI_Sendrecv with pinned buffers, then copy back to device ghost cells, overlapping this exchange with interior computation for performance.\n\nFor the mu computation, boundary z-planes need c ghost values while interior planes only need local c, so I can split the kernel: compute interior mu first while the c-halo exchange is still in flight, then handle boundary planes once ghosts arrive. The same staged approach applies to the mu halo exchange before the final cnew update, letting me overlap communication with interior-plane computation at each stage.\n\nI realize the cnew boundary planes actually depend on mu ghosts, so I need to restructure the step ordering: compute interior mu first, exchange c boundary planes while that runs, then compute boundary mu once the c ghosts arrive, exchange mu boundaries, and only then run the interior update kernel, chaining each stage with stream events so compute and transfers overlap properly.\n\nThe c boundary data should be ready since the previous step's update boundary kernel already completed, so the host just needs to wait on that event before issuing the D2H for c boundary. I'm also thinking about how the write to cnew factors into this sequencing.\n\nTracing through the dependency chain more carefully: cold isn't rewritten during this step so there's no conflict there, and the ghost c buffers being H2D'd on one stream don't interfere with the interior mu kernel since it only reads interior cold planes. The boundary mu kernel reads ghost c planes and correctly waits on the appropriate event, so that's fine too. Checking the mu plane indexing next, I confirm interior updates only touch local planes (0 to nzl-1) rather than the ghost planes at -1 and nzl, except at the very edge where plane 0's update needs the ghost plane.\n\nFor memory layout, I'm allocating arrays with extra ghost planes padding each side, then working out the clamping logic for domain boundaries — at global z=0 or the top boundary, the Laplacian should use the center value instead of reaching into a nonexistent ghost plane. I'm defining per-rank flags for whether a rank owns the low or high global boundary, so the kernel knows when to clamp to self rather than reading the neighbor plane.\n\nI also need to handle x and y boundaries the same way with simple min/max clamping, and I need to guard against the edge case where there are more MPI ranks than z-planes, which would leave some ranks with zero planes — that should just trigger an error exit.\n\nThinking through how to handle more ranks than z-planes: I could split off idle ranks into a separate communicator using MPI_Comm_split with MPI_UNDEFINED, letting active ranks do all the real work while idle ones get MPI_COMM_NULL and exit cleanly.\n\nFor non-divisible z counts, I'll let slab sizes differ by at most one plane, keeping x,y undecomposed since full planes are contiguous and GPU-friendly.\n\nNow I'm planning the compute kernels — launching a 3D grid where blockIdx.z maps to plane index and each thread handles one (x,y) cell, with the mu kernel taking pointers to padded concentration and mu arrays plus grid dimensions, plane range, boundary clamp flags, and physical parameters like gamma and the pairwise energies, making sure spacing values like dx*dx are computed identically to preserve numerical equivalence.\n\nTo guarantee bit-for-bit matching between CUDA and host, I need to disable fused multiply-add on both compilers and confirm division stays IEEE-compliant on the GPU by avoiding fast-math flags, since even reordering via FMA would shift results slightly. I'm also tracing through the exact left-to-right parsing of the mu formula — confirming how the sum of the pairwise energy term, the cubic term, and the gamma-laplacian term associate in C++ — so I can reproduce it verbatim in device code without introducing any reordering.\n\nNow I'm thinking about whether I need a shared host/device function for this expression, and realizing the real structural question: using OpenMP for host-side work like initialization, and handling the fact that validation and result printing need the full grid gathered onto rank 0 via contiguous MPI_Gatherv since slabs are already in z-major order. I'm weighing whether to do distributed min/max reduction versus gathering everything first, given that validation needs NaN/min/max checks across the whole field just for the printed concentration range.\n\nI'm deciding to split the approach: distributed MPI_Allreduce for validation stats (since min/max/NaN reduce exactly the same way distributed), but still gather the full array for print_results since that needs a hash over the whole dataset. Now I'm considering where OpenMP best fits in this hybrid design — host-side initialization, host-side reductions, or actually splitting compute work between CPU threads and GPU to get genuine hybrid performance gains.\n\nSince this is an accelerator-focused cluster, adding CPU compute co-processing would add too much complexity around halo transfers for a CPU-side slab, so I'll keep OpenMP strictly host-side: initialization, validation reductions, and the gather/copy work, while the GPU handles the actual stencil compute since the problem is memory-bandwidth-bound and GPU-dominant anyway.\n\nI'm also mapping MPI ranks to GPUs using a shared-memory communicator split to find local rank, then calling cudaSetDevice based on that; timing stays on high_resolution_clock with barriers around the compute loop to preserve the original MCUPS and \"Computation time\" output format, with rank 0 printing all status messages. For validation and the -r flag, I'll gather the full vector to rank 0 and reuse the existing templated print_results function, keeping everything in the single cahn_hilliard.cpp file with CMake configured for CXX and CUDA languages.\n\nSince I can't add new files, I need to compile the whole cahn_hilliard.cpp as CUDA by forcing its language property to CUDA so nvcc handles both the MPI host code and the embedded `__global__` kernels — nvcc's host compiler should tolerate the MPI headers fine. For ghost planes, I'm leaving them zero initially since they'll get filled by the halo exchange, which I'm implementing with paired MPI_Sendrecv calls between neighboring ranks (using MPI_PROC_NULL at domain boundaries) to swap top and bottom planes with distinct tags.\n\nNow I'm working through the staging buffers for the halo exchange: pinned host buffers for sending and receiving planes, with device-to-host copies of the boundary planes, MPI_Sendrecv calls to swap with neighbors, then host-to-device copies into the ghost regions. I'm also reasoning about stream ordering using CUDA events so the exchange happens after the producing kernel finishes and before the consumer kernel that needs the ghost data runs, and thinking through how this applies similarly to the mu field's boundary kernels.\n\nOnce that's done, host syncs sx for the D2H transfer of cold boundary planes, runs the MPI exchange, then copies ghosts back to device and records an event so the compute stream can launch boundary and interior mu kernels in order. The design:\n\n- **MPI**: 1D slab decomposition along z, with host-staged halo exchange of contiguous planes.\n- **CUDA**: stencil kernels for chemical potential and update, with streams and events so the interior kernel overlaps the halo transfers.\n- **OpenMP**: host-side initialization and validation reductions.","time":{"start":1793043284014,"end":1793043284033}}}

Halo transfers are overlapped with\n//              interior kernels using streams and events.\n//   * OpenMP - host-side work: parallel field initialization and parallel\n//              min/max/NaN reductions used for validation.\n//\n// Arithmetic is performed in exactly the same order as the serial reference\n// implementation (and FMA contraction is disabled), so the computed field is\n// bit-for-bit identical to the original code for any decomposition.\n\n#include <algorithm>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <limits>\n#include <utility>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include <cuda_runtime.h>\n#include <mpi.h>\n#include <omp.h>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\n#define CUDA_CHECK(call)                                                          \\\n    do {                                                                          \\\n        cudaError_t err_ = (call);                                                \\\n        if (err_ != cudaSuccess) {                                                \\\n            fprintf(stderr, \"CUDA error at %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__,      \\\n                    cudaGetErrorString(err_));                                    \\\n            MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);                                         \\\n        }                                                                         \\\n    } while (0)\n\n// 3D index calculation\ninline constexpr size_t idx3(const size_t x, const size_t y, const size_t z, const size_t nx, const size_t ny) noexcept {\n    return z * (nx * ny) + y * nx + x;\n}\n\nnamespace {\n\nconstexpr int TAG_UP = 100;\nconstexpr int TAG_DOWN = 101;\nconstexpr unsigned BLOCK_X = 32;\nconstexpr unsigned BLOCK_Y = 8;\nconstexpr int MAX_GRID_Z = 65535;\n\nstruct Physics {\n    double dx, dy, dz, dt, e_AA, e_BB, e_AB, gamma, D;\n};\n\nstruct Options {\n    size_t nx = 64;\n    size_t ny = 0;\n    size_t nz = 0;\n    int iterations = 20;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n};\n\n// Clamped Laplacian of a field stored in padded z-slab layout.\n// pc / pm / pp are element offsets of the centre, lower and upper z-planes.\n// Clamping at the global domain edges is expressed by pm == pc or pp == pc,\n// which reproduces the original (c[z] + c[z] - 2 c[z]) boundary treatment.\n__device__ __forceinline__ double laplacianDevice(const double* __restrict__ f, const size_t pc, const size_t pm,\n                                                  const size_t pp, const int x, const int y, const int nx,\n                                                  const int ny, const double dx, const double dy, const double dz) {\n    const int xp = (x < nx - 1) ? x + 1 : x;\n    const int yp = (y < ny - 1) ? y + 1 : y;\n    const int xn = (x > 0) ? x - 1 : 0;\n    const int yn = (y > 0) ? y - 1 : 0;\n\n    const size_t row = static_cast<size_t>(y) * nx;\n    const double center = f[pc + row + x];\n\n    const double cxx = (f[pc + row + xp] + f[pc + row + xn] - 2.0 * center) / (dx * dx);\n    const double cyy = (f[pc + static_cast<size_t>(yp) * nx + x] + f[pc + static_cast<size_t>(yn) * nx + x] -\n                        2.0 * center) / (dy * dy);\n    const double czz = (f[pp + row + x] + f[pm + row + x] - 2.0 * center) / (dz * dz);\n\n    return cxx + cyy + czz;\n}\n\n// Chemical potential on local z-planes [k0, k0 + kcount) of the slab.\n__global__ void chemPotKernel(const double* __restrict__ c, double* __restrict__ mu, const int nx, const int ny,\n                              const int nzl, const int k0, const int kcount, const int clampLo, const int clampHi,\n                              const double dx, const double dy, const double dz, const double gamma,\n                              const double e_AA, const double e_BB, const double e_AB) {\n    const int x = static_cast<int>(blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x);\n    const int y = static_cast<int>(blockIdx.y * blockDim.y + threadIdx.y);\n    if (x >= nx || y >= ny) return;\n\n    const size_t plane = static_cast<size_t>(nx) * ny;\n    for (int kk = blockIdx.z; kk < kcount; kk += gridDim.z) {\n        const int k = k0 + kk;\n        const size_t pc = static_cast<size_t>(k + 1) * plane;  // +1 skips the lower ghost plane\n        const size_t pm = (k == 0 && clampLo) ? pc : pc - plane;\n        const size_t pp = (k == nzl - 1 && clampHi) ? pc : pc + plane;\n\n        const size_t i = pc + static_cast<size_t>(y) * nx + x;\n        const double cv = c[i];\n        const double lap = laplacianDevice(c, pc, pm, pp, x, y, nx, ny, dx, dy, dz);\n\n        mu[i] = 4.5 * ((cv + 1.0) * e_AA + (cv - 1.0) * e_BB - 2.0 * cv * e_AB)\n                + 3.0 * cv + cv * cv * cv\n                - gamma * lap;\n    }\n}\n\n// Cahn-Hilliard update on local z-planes [k0, k0 + kcount) of the slab.\n__global__ void updateKernel(double* __restrict__ cnew, const double* __restrict__ cold,\n                             const double* __restrict__ mu, const int nx, const int ny, const int nzl,\n                             const int k0, const int kcount, const int clampLo, const int clampHi,\n                             const double D, const double dt, const double dx, const double dy, const double dz) {\n    const int x = static_cast<int>(blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x);\n    const int y = static_cast<int>(blockIdx.y * blockDim.y + threadIdx.y);\n    if (x >= nx || y >= ny) return;\n\n    const size_t plane = static_cast<size_t>(nx) * ny;\n    for (int kk = blockIdx.z; kk < kcount; kk += gridDim.z) {\n        const int k = k0 + kk;\n        const size_t pc = static_cast<size_t>(k + 1) * plane;\n        const size_t pm = (k == 0 && clampLo) ? pc : pc - plane;\n        const size_t pp = (k == nzl - 1 && clampHi) ? pc : pc + plane;\n\n        const size_t i = pc + static_cast<size_t>(y) * nx + x;\n        cnew[i] = cold[i] + dt * D * laplacianDevice(mu, pc, pm, pp, x, y, nx, ny, dx, dy, dz);\n    }\n}\n\nvoid launchChemPot(const double* d_c, double* d_mu, const int nx, const int ny, const int nzl, const int k0,\n                   const int kcount, const bool clampLo, const bool clampHi, const Physics& p, cudaStream_t s) {\n    if (kcount <= 0) return;\n    const dim3 block(BLOCK_X, BLOCK_Y);\n    const dim3 grid((nx + BLOCK_X - 1) / BLOCK_X, (ny + BLOCK_Y - 1) / BLOCK_Y,\n                    std::min(kcount, MAX_GRID_Z));\n    chemPotKernel<<<grid, block, 0, s>>>(d_c, d_mu, nx, ny, nzl, k0, kcount, clampLo ? 1 : 0, clampHi ? 1 : 0,\n                                         p.dx, p.dy, p.dz, p.gamma, p.e_AA, p.e_BB, p.e_AB);\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n}\n\nvoid launchUpdate(double* d_cnew, const double* d_cold, const double* d_mu, const int nx, const int ny,\n                  const int nzl, const int k0, const int kcount, const bool clampLo, const bool clampHi,\n                  const Physics& p, cudaStream_t s) {\n    if (kcount <= 0) return;\n    const dim3 block(BLOCK_X, BLOCK_Y);\n    const dim3 grid((nx + BLOCK_X - 1) / BLOCK_X, (ny + BLOCK_Y - 1) / BLOCK_Y,\n                    std::min(kcount, MAX_GRID_Z));\n    updateKernel<<<grid, block, 0, s>>>(d_cnew, d_cold, d_mu, nx, ny, nzl, k0, kcount, clampLo ? 1 : 0,\n                                        clampHi ? 1 : 0, p.D, p.dt, p.dx, p.dy, p.dz);\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n}\n\n// Communication state for exchanging ghost planes of a device field.\nstruct Halo {\n    MPI_Comm comm;\n    int lo;  // neighbour {"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793043333219,"sessionID":"ses_e864d951fffeCCx8jlVTj30uFv","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_01Fw6krxowUi1SJftnqRNnRL","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/cahn-hilliard_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r3/cahn-hilliard/CMakeLists.txt","content":"cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.24)\nproject(cahn_hilliard_benchmark LANGUAGES CXX CUDA)\n\nset(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)\nset(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)\nset(CMAKE_CUDA_STANDARD 20)\nset(CMAKE_CUDA_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)\n\n# Target GPU architecture(s); override with -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=<list> for a cluster build.\nif(NOT DEFINED CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES)\n    set(CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES native)\nendif()\n\nfind_package(MPI REQUIRED COMPONENTS CXX)\nfind_package(OpenMP REQUIRED COMPONENTS CXX)\nfind_package(CUDAToolkit REQUIRED)\n\n# The solver contains CUDA kernels, so the translation unit is compiled by nvcc.\nset_source_files_properties(cahn_hilliard.cpp PROPERTIES LANGUAGE CUDA)\nadd_executable(cahn_hilliard cahn_hilliard.cpp)\n\n# Optimizations. FMA contraction is disabled on both host and device so that\n# results are bit-identical to the serial reference implementation.\ntarget_compile_options(cahn_hilliard PRIVATE\n    $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CUDA>:--fmad=false>\n    $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CUDA>:-Xcompiler=-O3>\n    $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CUDA>:-Xcompiler=-march=native>\n    $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CUDA>:-Xcompiler=-ffp-contract=off>\n    $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CUDA>:-Xcompiler=-Wall>\n    $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CUDA>:-Xcompiler=-Wextra>\n    $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CUDA>:-Xcompiler=-fopenmp>\n)\ntarget_compile_options(cahn_hilliard PRIVATE $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CUDA>:-O3>)\n\n# MPI, OpenMP, CUDA runtime, and math library\ntarget_link_libraries(cahn_hilliard PRIVATE\n    MPI::MPI_CXX\n    OpenMP::OpenMP_CXX\n    CUDA::cudart\n    m\n)\n"},"output":"Wrote file successfully.","metadata":{"diagnostics":{},"filepath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/cahn-hilliard_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r3/cahn-hilliard/CMakeLists.txt","exists":true,"truncated":false},"title":"home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/cahn-hilliard_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r3/cahn-hilliard/CMakeLists.txt","time":{"start":1793043333155,"end":1793043333179}},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"caller":{"type":"direct"}}},"id":"prt_179b5f6f5001znMa25B9h8t9hN","sessionID":"ses_e864d951fffeCCx8jlVTj30uFv","messageID":"msg_179b5eb02001n09gS6D77IrQ6F"}}
